visual_standard.rule: Every post teaches a useful business lesson about interactive websites, product launches, 3D scroll experiences, or product storytelling. No project-asset filler.

carousels.campaign_goal: Explain what an interactive website should do for a buyer.
carousels.lesson: Interaction should capture attention, explain the offer, sustain engagement, and make the next action clearer.
carousels.caption:
An interactive website should do more than look different.

The job is to make the offer easier to understand and the experience easier to remember.

A useful interaction has a purpose: capture attention, explain the product, keep the buyer engaged, then make the next action obvious.

That is the difference between adding motion and designing an experience.

carousels.campaign_goal: Teach the structure of a strong digital product launch.
carousels.lesson: A launch experience should move from positioning to design, interaction, and a clear launch path.
carousels.caption:
A product launch site is not just a homepage with a new product on it.

The experience needs a sequence.

Start with the reason to care. Show the product clearly. Reveal the details that justify the value. Use interaction where it improves understanding. Then give the buyer a clear next step.

Good launch design turns information into a story people can follow.

carousels.campaign_goal: Teach why website motion should have a business purpose.
carousels.lesson: Motion should help a buyer understand the product or next action instead of existing as decoration.
carousels.caption:
Motion is not the strategy.

A useful website interaction should help a buyer understand something faster: what the product does, why it matters, how it works, or what to do next.

If the animation cannot answer one of those questions, it may be decoration rather than communication.

carousels.campaign_goal: Explain when 3D adds real value to a website.
carousels.lesson: 3D is most useful when depth helps explain scale, construction, function, or configuration.
carousels.caption:
A 3D website needs a reason to be 3D.

Depth is useful when it helps people understand scale, construction, function, configuration, or a detail that a flat image cannot communicate as clearly.

The goal is not to make an object spin. The goal is to make the product easier to understand.

carousels.campaign_goal: Teach the information sequence behind a clear product launch.
carousels.lesson: A launch should answer why the buyer should care, what the product is, why it is better, and what to do next.
carousels.caption:
A strong product launch answers questions in the order the buyer experiences them.

Why should I care?
What is it?
Why is it better?
What do I do next?

When a launch experience answers those questions clearly, design and interaction have a job instead of becoming noise.
